title: Gràcia: Streets and Green Space
subtitle: A district of Barcelona, measured from OpenStreetMap

sources.text: (c) OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL 1.0), retrieved via the Overpass API and clipped to the district boundary from Nominatim

claims.text: The district has 91.9 km of mapped streets.
26.7 km of them are living streets.
Parks, gardens and playgrounds cover 134 acres.
Every school is within 400 m of a park.
Travessera de Gràcia follows the street grid.

sections.title: The district at a glance
sections.intro: Gràcia is one of the densest districts of Barcelona, and its streets decide how much room is left for green space.

slides.title: A fine web of streets
slides.body: The district has 91.9 km of mapped streets, and 26.7 km of them are living streets where pedestrians come first.

slides.title: A regular grid
slides.body: Travessera de Gràcia runs 0.4 degrees off the dominant direction of the street grid, so it follows the grid rather than cutting across it.

sections.title: Green space and daily life
sections.intro: Small gardens and playgrounds do much of the work that large parks do elsewhere.

slides.title: Small parks, everywhere
slides.body: Parks, gardens and playgrounds cover 134 acres of the district.

slides.title: Schools next to green space
slides.body: There are 40 schools, and every one is within 400 m of a park.
